ATTENDANCE:         Johan Lopez, Chair (approx. 6:04 p.m.); Richard Dellinger, Vice

STAFF:              Jodi Trendler

CALL TO ORDER 
Vice Chair Dellinger called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m. 

ROLL CALL 
Vice Chair Dellinger acknowledged those present. Chair Lopez joined and assumed the 
chair. 

PUBLIC COMMENTS 
No public participation.  

ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES - October 14, 2026 
** MR. DELLINGER MADE A MOTION TO ACCEPT THE OCTOBER 14, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING MINUTES. 
** MOTION PASSED (MR. LOPEZ ABSTAINED).  

NEW BUSINESS 
Ms. Trendler presented the Norwalk 2050 Sustainability and Resilience Roadmap. She 
said she would submit the final roadmap to the Mayor on November 9 and share a link 
with the committee afterward. The committee took no formal action. 
Vice Chair Dellinger resumed presiding after Chair Lopez departed. 

ADJOURNMENT 
** MR. DELLINGER MADE A MOTION TO ADJOURN. 
** MOTION PASSED UNANIMOUSLY.  
 
The meeting adjourned at approximately 7:21 p.m. 
 
Respectfully Submitted, 
Courtney Baldwin 
Recording Secretary  
 
 Norwalk 2050 
Sustainability and 
Resilience Roadmap
Roadmap Overview
Ad Hoc Sustainability and Resilience Committee
November 2026It began with a question

What does it mean for Norwalk to be a “green” city?

Over the first eight months of the Roadmap process, the City listened before it planned.

                                                                    The answer: A city that is
          City Green Team
          Department staff shared what green means for City 
          services.
                                                                          Vibrant              Resilient
          Community task force
          Residents, businesses, and subject matter experts 
          shared knowledge and lived experience.
                                                                      Regenerative           Sustainable
          Community tabling events
          Residents across neighborhoods shared what matters 
          most in their daily lives.                                This became the Roadmap’s central 
                                                                    objective.


    Norwalk 2050 Sustainability and Resilience Roadmap                                                         2The objective: Vibrant, Resilient, Regenerative, Sustainable

  Vibrant                                                  Resilient
  Strong current conditions and opportunities that let residents, Able to anticipate, absorb, and adapt to environmental, 
  businesses, and institutions flourish; the quality that makes economic, or social disruptions while keeping essential 
  people want to live, work, invest, and visit.            functions and continuing to evolve.

  2050 vision: Every neighborhood is a healthy, connected, 2050 vision: Residents, businesses, buildings, natural 
  welcoming place, with quality jobs, affordable housing, healthy systems, and critical services prepare for, withstand, and 
  food, parks, cultural life, and safe ways to get around. recover quickly from floods, heat, storms, and outages, and no 
                                                           household faces disruption alone.

  Regenerative                                             Sustainable
  Actively restores and improves ecological, economic, and Meets present needs while ensuring adequate resources 
  social systems so they function better over time, rather than remain for future generations, through long-term stewardship of 
  simply preventing further harm.                          environmental, economic, and social systems.

  2050 vision: Rivers, the harbor, wetlands, tree canopy, and 2050 vision: Norwalk reaches net-zero greenhouse gas 
  open space are restored and managed as core infrastructure, emissions, keeps materials in productive use, invests within its 
  while local wealth and community capacity grow in every  means, and maintains its restored systems for future 
  neighborhood.                                            generations.

Source: Norwalk 2050 Roadmap Introduction, Table 1.1, VRRS Matrix. Every chapter and strategy option is evaluated through these four lenses.

    Norwalk 2050 Sustainability and Resilience Roadmap                                                         3A 23-year guide for a vibrant, resilient Norwalk

2050. It helps the City and its partners coordinate 
decisions across departments and sectors, with limited               years, 2027 to 2050

    Norwalk 2050 Sustainability and Resilience Roadmap                                                        10Global focus has shifted to limiting 1.5°C overshoot

September 2026
                                                        Global emission cuts needed from 
UNEP’s Limiting Overshoot report found that exceeding 1.5°C 2025 levels on the lowest-overshoot 
of warming is now unavoidable. The priority is limiting how high pathway
temperatures rise and how long they stay above 1.5°C.
October 2026                                            18%              by 2030
UNEP’s Emissions Gap Report found the lowest remaining 
pathway peaks at 1.7 to 1.8°C around mid-century and returns 
to 1.5°C by 2100. Current policies point toward about 2.8°C. 45%         by 2035
What it means
Every five years of emissions at current levels adds about 
0.1°C to peak warming. Faster near-term reductions reduce 69%            by 2040
long-term risk and cost.


Sources: UNEP, Limiting Overshoot (September 2026); UNEP, Emissions Gap Report 2026: The Point of Return (October 2026).

    Norwalk 2050 Sustainability and Resilience Roadmap                                                16What residents and neighbors can do

           At home:                                                 Getting around:  
           Reduce energy use 4% per year                            Reduce Car trips 15% per week 
        •  Get a home energy assessment and weatherize             •  Walk, bike, or take the bus for short trips –
           through HeatSmart Norwalk to plan for a heat               Start with once a week
           pump before the furnace or boiler fails
                                                                   •  Make the next car electric - CHEAPR 
        •  Reduce energy:  LEDs, Smart strips, Energy                 Rebates
           Star appliances, programmable thermostat
                                                                   •  Use commuter and transit programs where 
        •  Consider rooftop solar                                     available

           Every day                                                Together
          •   Reduce waste 4% per year, reuse, recycle             •  Join group campaigns like Solarize and 
              correctly, and compost                                  HeatSmart
          •   Plant and care for trees                             •  Check on neighbors in heat waves and storms
          •   Make a household emergency plan                      •  Get to know your neighbors!
          •   Grow your own food & eat less meat

Most household actions also lower energy bills, improve health and comfort, and make homes safer.
